events.did: scrawled a formula on the digital white board and explained carbon bonds to her class
events.quote_anchor: As her hand scrawled out a formula on the digital white board, and her mouth rattled off an explanation about carbon bonds,

events.did: asked the class for questions before the bell rang
events.quote_anchor: “Any questions?” she asked, but she’d timed the words well.

events.did: slid her notes back in her bag and started for the door as the students surged up
events.quote_anchor: She slid her notes back in her bag and started for the door.

events.did: called after her asking to ask a question, and she kept walking
events.quote_anchor: “Could I ask a question?” pressed the student. Dani tugged the tie out of her hair, shook out her black curls,

events.did: rubbed her temples, unlocked her office door, and stopped when she saw the room wasn't empty
events.quote_anchor: Dani rubbed her temples, and unlocked her office door, and stopped abruptly when she saw that the room wasn’t empty.

events.did: asked the man in her office how he got in
events.quote_anchor: “The name’s on the door,” she said, too tired to beat around the bush. “How did you get in?”

events.did: recognized the small round object in the man's hand as an inhaler with a brightly glowing blue liquid
events.quote_anchor: she saw one hand was fidgeting with a small round object. It took her a moment to recognize the disc for what it was: an inhaler.

events.did: twitched his mouth into a smile without warmth and said he certainly hoped he could help
events.quote_anchor: The stranger’s mouth twitched, a smile without any of the warmth. “For both our sakes,” he said, “I certainly hope so.”

relations.did: tensed, knowing she had never seen this man before and that he was not a professor in her department
relations.quote_anchor: Dani tensed. She might not know her students’ names, but she knew their faces well enough to know she’d never seen this man before.

relations.did: sat waiting at her desk on her own side, his back to the cabinets and his gaze on the door
relations.quote_anchor: A man sat waiting at her desk, not on the student side, but on her own, his back to the cabinets and his gaze on the door.

relations.did: seemed unbothered by her question and did not answer it
relations.quote_anchor: The man seemed unbothered by the question, but he didn’t answer.

relations.did: heard her mother and friends asking what happened, when they meant to ask what she had done to screw it up
relations.quote_anchor: What happened? when what they meant to say was What did you do to screw that up?

numbers.did: had sixty-eight students in her current block
numbers.quote_anchor: There were sixty-eight students in her current block. It was pointless trying to learn their names.

numbers.did: had already given the same lecture five times in the three years she had been stuck teaching sophomores
numbers.quote_anchor: she’d already given five times in the three years she’d been stuck teaching sophomores.

numbers.did: had been on track three years ago to be the first Black female chemist at the country's most prestigious lab
numbers.quote_anchor: Three years ago, Dani had been on track to be the first Black female chemist at the country’s most prestigious lab.

numbers.did: counted a hot bath, a tall glass of wine and some shitty reality TV as three components of her disassociation
numbers.quote_anchor: some shitty reality TV, three components that formed the stable structure of her disassociation.

numbers.did: said half of her students would drop over the course of the semester
numbers.quote_anchor: Even at a school as good as Lockland, half of them would drop over the course of the semester—it was only a question of when.

numbers.did: told Dani that her question wouldn't take a long
numbers.quote_anchor: “I know,” said the student, “but it won’t take a long and—”
